Package info.openrocket.core.simulation.listeners

Interface SimulationListener

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractSimulationListener, EnsembleRunListener, FlightControllerSimulatorListener, MotorBatchRunner.TrialListener
public interface SimulationListener
Listen to simulation events and possibly take action. If the implementation maintains any state, it should be properly cloned.

    • startSimulation

      void startSimulation(SimulationStatus status) throws info.openrocket.core.simulation.exception.SimulationException

    • endSimulation

      void endSimulation(SimulationStatus status, info.openrocket.core.simulation.exception.SimulationException exception)
      Called when ending a simulation. This is called either when the simulation ends normally (due to an end simulation event) or when a SimulationException is thrown.

      This method cannot throw a SimulationException, since the simulation is already being ended.

      Parameters:
      status - the simulation status.
      exception - the exception that caused ending the simulation, or null if ending normally.

    • preStep

      boolean preStep(SimulationStatus status) throws info.openrocket.core.simulation.exception.SimulationException
      Called before a simulation step is taken. This method may also prevent the normal stepping method from being called.
      Parameters:
      status - the simulation status.
      Returns:
      true to continue normally, false to skip taking the step
      Throws:
      info.openrocket.core.simulation.exception.SimulationException

    • postStep

      void postStep(SimulationStatus status) throws info.openrocket.core.simulation.exception.SimulationException
      Called immediately after a simulation step has been taken. This method is called whether the preStep(SimulationStatus) aborted the step or not.
      Parameters:
      status - the simulation status.
      Throws:
      info.openrocket.core.simulation.exception.SimulationException

    • isSystemListener

      boolean isSystemListener()
      Return whether this is a system listener. System listeners are used internally for various purposes by OpenRocket. User-written listeners should always return false.

      System listeners do not cause warnings to be added to the simulation results when they affect the simulation.

      Returns:
      whether this is a system listener
